original_question: For measure differential equations on a manifold, where the non-variational setting uses probability vector fields that have only an abelian monoid structure rather than a Lie algebra structure, can one develop a mathematically useful control theory at the level of the induced flows instead of at the level of solutions, by leveraging geometric control techniques?
target_in_paper: Section 5.1, immediately after eq. (41): "We note that this approach allows for uniqueness at the level of solutions, thus opening the door to control problems. On the other side, if one wants to use a non-variational interpretation, then the setting of MDEs suffers from the fact that PVFs enjoy only a structure of abelian monoid and not of Lie algebra. A possibility is to explore control properties at the level of the flows, instead of solutions, taking advantage of the geometric control techniques [106]."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact MDE/PVF setting, the non-variational obstruction that probability vector fields have only an abelian-monoid structure rather than a Lie-algebra structure, and the paper’s proposed shift from solution-level control to flow-level control using geometric control ideas. It also correctly keeps the problem tied to measure differential equations on a manifold rather than drifting to broader Wasserstein control problems.
missing_details: The paper’s object is the specific measure differential equation mu_dot = V[mu], not a generic measure-valued control system.
A probability vector field must be defined explicitly as a map V: P(M) -> P(TM) satisfying pi_# V(mu) = mu.
The MDE is interpreted in the weak sense: for test functions f, d/dt int_M f dmu(t) = int_TM nabla_x f · v dV[mu(t)](x,v).
The nearby context contrasts this open direction with the variational/dissipative-PVF framework based on the functional W(V,W) in eq. (41), where uniqueness at the level of solutions is available.
The paper phrases the goal narrowly as to "explore control properties" at the level of flows; saying "develop a mathematically useful control theory" is a modest broadening beyond the text.
The flow in question is the flow/semigroup generated by the MDE, not the solution concepts for the continuity equations and differential inclusions discussed earlier in Section 4.5.

The paper does not specify an admissible control class, a cost functional, a controllability notion, or a concrete Lie-bracket-style criterion; adding any of these would go beyond the stated open problem.
No extra hypotheses on the manifold M are imposed in this passage, so the refined question should not add compactness, Euclidean structure, or other assumptions absent from the paper.
refined_question: Let M be a manifold, let P(M) be the space of probability measures on M, and let V: P(M) -> P(TM) be a probability vector field satisfying pi_# V(mu) = mu. For the measure differential equation mu_dot = V[mu], understood weakly by d/dt int_M f dmu(t) = int_TM nabla_x f · v dV[mu(t)](x,v), can one, in the non-variational interpretation where probability vector fields have only an abelian-monoid structure rather than a Lie-algebra structure, explore control properties at the level of the associated flows instead of at the level of individual solutions, by using geometric control techniques?
justification: The draft is clearly paraphrasing the future-direction sentence in Section 5.1 that follows the definition of MDEs and the discussion of uniqueness via the functional W(V,W). The nearby context defines the notation mu_dot = V[mu], the PVF condition pi_# V(mu) = mu, and the weak formulation of solutions, while Section 4.5 provides the broader background on existing control approaches for time-evolving measures. To stay paper-faithful, the question should therefore remain an exploratory flow-level control problem for MDEs, not a broader or more fully specified control theory for general measure dynamics.
